Planning a week of affordable, nutritious family dinners doesn’t have to be a source of stress or a drain on your wallet. With a little strategic thinking and a focus on versatile ingredients, you can serve delicious meals that nourish your family without breaking the bank. The key lies in simplifying your approach, embracing seasonal produce, and mastering the art of batch cooking.

Start by auditing your pantry and freezer. Before you head to the store, check what you already have. Staples like rice, lentils, canned beans, and frozen vegetables are nutritional powerhouses that are incredibly cheap. Building meals around these base ingredients ensures you’re not wasting money on fresh produce that might spoil before you get to it. When you do shop, stick to a strict list to avoid impulse buys. Focus on whole foods rather than processed items, which are often more expensive and less healthy.

Next, plan your menu with efficiency in mind. Aim for "mix-and-match" meals where ingredients overlap. For example, if you’re making chicken tacos on Tuesday, use the leftover chicken in a stir-fry on Thursday or a salad on Friday. This reduces waste and saves time.
